name: The Narts
note: The heroic race at the center of the Caucasian Nart epic; surviving Scytho-Sarmatian-Alanic mythology attested in Ossetian, Circassian, Abkhaz and other oral versions (Colarusso 2002; Dumézil).

name: Batraz
note: Steel-tempered chief warrior-hero of the Narts; Dumézil reads him as a Scytho-Sarmatian war-god whose steel sword cast into the sea continues the Scythian sword-cult of Herodotus's Ares (Colarusso 2002; Dumézil).

name: Satana
note: Wise matriarch and counselor of the Narts, sister-consort within the central Nart family; Dumézil links her name to a Sarmatian/Alanic prototype (Colarusso 2002).

name: Uastyrdzhi
note: Ossetian rider-god and patron of warriors and travelers, syncretized with Saint George; venerated at the festival Jeoryguba (Dumézil; Colarusso 2002).

name: Sosruko
note: Trickster culture-hero (Ossetian Soslan/Sozyryko; Circassian Sosruko) born from stone, tempered like steel, famed for the theft of fire (Colarusso 2002; Dumézil).

name: Syrdon
note: Malicious trickster of the Narts, sower of discord and inventor of the twelve-string harp from the bones of his slain sons; the standard scholarly Loki-analogue (Colarusso 2002; Dumézil).

name: Kurdalagon
note: Heavenly smith of the Nart cosmos who tempers heroes (Batraz, Soslan) in his forge as one tempers steel (Colarusso 2002; Dumézil).
